claims.claim: Same-seed training on CPU gave identical parameters; torch.load of a pickled model raised UnpicklingError; a dict of state dicts, epoch and torch.get_rng_state() loaded with the default.
claims.source: Run with torch 2.14.0 (CPU) in a scratch environment for this repository.

claims.claim: PyTorch recommends a worker_init_fn seeding NumPy and random from torch.initial_seed(), and CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG for deterministic CUDA.
claims.source: PyTorch documentation, Reproducibility notes (not reachable from this environment).

concept_html:
Neural network training draws random numbers everywhere: weight initialisation, data shuffling, dropout, augmentation. Control every source and two runs with the same seed give the same weights. In this course's build (PyTorch 2.14, CPU), a small network trained twice with seed 1 produced identical parameters. Seed 2 produced different ones.

Seed at the entry point, once. Your own code takes generators as parameters (lesson B6-L1). Libraries and PyTorch internals use global generators, so seed those too, at the start of the training script:

random.seed(seed)
np.random.seed(seed)
torch.manual_seed(seed)                       # CPU and all CUDA devices
loader_gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
train_loader = DataLoader(ds, batch_size=64, shuffle=True, generator=loader_gen)
  • Pass a seeded generator to every shuffling DataLoader, so batch order is fixed.
  • With num_workers > 0, the PyTorch documentation recommends a worker_init_fn that seeds NumPy and random in each worker from torch.initial_seed().
  • torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True) makes PyTorch raise an error for operations that have no deterministic implementation, instead of silently varying. On CUDA it also needs the CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG environment variable, as the documentation describes.

Exact equality holds for the same code, library versions and hardware. Across GPU models or library versions, expect small differences, and compare metrics within a tolerance (lesson B14-L3).

Checkpoints let a long run resume and let you keep the best epoch. Save a dict of state, not the model object:

torch.save({"model": model.state_dict(), "optimizer": optimizer.state_dict(),
            "epoch": epoch, "torch_rng": torch.get_rng_state()}, path)

torch.load loads weights only by default in PyTorch 2.14. A checkpoint holding a pickled model object fails with UnpicklingError. That default protects you: loading an arbitrary pickle can execute code. Save state dicts, rebuild the model class in code, and load the weights into it.

lines: import random
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import torch
def seed_everything(seed: int) -> torch.Generator:
"""Seed Python, NumPy and PyTorch global state; return a generator for DataLoaders."""
random.seed(seed)
np.random.seed(seed)
torch.manual_seed(seed)
return torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
def save_checkpoint(path: Path, model: torch.nn.Module, optimizer: torch.optim.Optimizer, epoch: int) -> None:
"""Save state dicts and RNG state, never the model object."""
torch.save(
{
"model": model.state_dict(),
"optimizer": optimizer.state_dict(),
"epoch": epoch,
"torch_rng": torch.get_rng_state(),
},
path,
)

import random

import numpy as np
import torch


def seed_everything(seed: int) -> torch.Generator:
    """Seed Python, NumPy and PyTorch global state at the entry point.

    Args:
        seed: The run's seed, logged with the run.

    Returns:
        A seeded generator to pass to shuffling DataLoaders.
    """
    random.seed(seed)
    np.random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    return torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)

title: Reproducible PyTorch runs and safe checkpoints
why_html: A team fine-tuned a classifier and reported 0.86 F1. A reviewer reran the notebook and got 0.83, then 0.85. The DataLoader shuffled with the global generator, dropout drew from it too, and an augmentation library used its own. Nobody could say which number was "the" result. Fixing the seeds and the loader generator made the run repeatable: 0.84, every time. The earlier 0.86 had been a lucky draw.
